sections.label: Deepfake reports in US and Singapore
sections.summary: It cites a 2024 US report on deepfakes in schools and November 2024 Singapore reports of students investigated for deepfake nude photos.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Centre for Democracy and Technology (CDT) in the US reported in 2024 that 40% of students and 29% of teachers were aware of a deepfake depicting individuals associated with their school being shared.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, reports in November 2024 emerged that students from one of our schools were investigated for deepfake nude photos of female classmates shared amongst WhatsApp groups, illustrating that we too are experiencing this problem.

sections.label: Penal Code AI deepfake amendments

sentences.text: MHA announced last year that there will be amendments to the Penal Code to make clear that our offences apply to sexually explicit deepfakes produced through AI and I would like to seek clarifications from the Minister on when we can expect these to be tabled.

sections.label: Motorcyclist, elderly, foreign worker accident shares
sections.summary: Motorcyclists and pillion riders were involved in 55.2% of traffic accidents and close to 60% of traffic fatalities, the elderly in 44% of pedestrian fatalities, and lorry accidents involving foreign workers saw three fatalities a year from 2020 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The elderly made up close to 12.5% of the population, but were involved in 44% of all pedestrian fatalities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Separately, accidents involving foreign workers on lorries have seen three fatalities a year, from 2020 to 2022.

sections.label: Racial Harmony Bill and self-radicalisation arrests
sections.summary: The House passed the Racial Harmony Bill, complementing earlier religious harmony legislation, yet self-radicalised people continue to be arrested under the Internal Security Act, most recently Singapore's first arrest for far-right extremism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At the last Sitting, this House passed the Racial Harmony Bill and this complements the earlier legislation we had in relation to religious harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the safeguards in place, we continue to see self-radicalised people getting arrested under the Internal Security Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The most recent was our first arrest for a person engaged in far-right extremism in Singapore.

sections.label: 2024 scam case and loss figures
sections.summary: In 2024, scam cases rose 10.6% to 51,501 and monies lost rose 70.6% to at least $1.1 billion, with WhatsApp, Telegram, Facebook and Tik Tok accounting for over half.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Recent figures report that in 2024, the number of scams alone, increased by 10.6% to 51,501 cases from 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Even more concerning is the report that the total amount of monies lost increased by 70.6% to at least $1.1 billion in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Scammers using platforms such as WhatsApp, Telegram, Facebook and Tik Tok account for more than half of all scams committed.

sections.label: Caning for scammers
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Minister for Home Affairs to allow caning for scammers, especially egregious cases, possibly mandatory caning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Because given this discrepancy, we need to harmonise and send a clear message.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I call upon the Minister for Home Affairs to allow caning as a punishment for scammers, especially the egregious cases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: One possible model for the most egregious cases, mandatory caning.

sections.label: Scam enforcement and rising losses
sections.summary: Anti-scam measures disrupted 45,000 activities and recovered $180 million, yet scam cases rose over 10% to around 50,000 and losses surged 70% to over $1.1 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The operationalisation of the Online Criminal Harms Act has disrupted over 45,000 online criminal activities, while the roll-out of enhanced anti-malware features on banking apps have contributed to 85% reduction in malware -enabled scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Targeted enforcement efforts led by the Anti-Scam Command have led to the freezing of over 21,000 bank accounts and the recovery of more than $180 million in scam proceeds, along with campaigns like "Add, Check, Tell" which were started to empower Singaporeans to recognise and report scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Yet, despite these strides, scam cases increased by more than 10% to around 50,000 and overall losses surged by a staggering 70% to more than $1.1 billion as compared to 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A particularly disturbing trend is the rise in scams involving "self-effected" transfers, which now account for over 80% of all scam reports.

sections.label: Fires involving active mobility devices
sections.summary: Overall fires rose 2% to almost 2,000 cases in 2024, with a 22% increase in fires involving active mobility devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While the overall number of fires rose by 2% to almost 2,000 cases in 2024, a worrying trend is the 22% increase in fires involving active mobility devices (AMDs).

sections.label: Home Team transformation commitment

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)

sections.label: Home Team manpower and technology
sections.summary: The passage asks about Home Team strategies to recruit and train Singaporeans for SCDF's EMS workforce and about raising public awareness of technology deployments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For the Minister, on our Home Team Manpower Resource, firstly, regarding recruitment and training of locals while Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) expands its Emergency Medical Services (EMS) workforce and aims to maintain a local core, what are the strategies by the Home Team to recruit and train more Singaporeans and work together possibly with our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) or mid-career switches so that SCDF will remain a career of choice in the face of growing competition for talent?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Thirdly, on augmenting Home Team workforce with technology, I know we are using smart and autonomous solutions more increasingly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, I feel that the Home Team also needs to increase public awareness on the deployment of these solutions to instill confidence and assurance in public that, while there is no visible officer, that does not mean that there is no security and vigilance.

sections.label: Re-integration Hubs and desistors
sections.summary: The passage asks about Re-integration Hubs supporting desistors before release, their number and locations, and efforts to encourage families in re-integration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister of State share more about the Re-integration Hubs and their role in supporting desistors before their release?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How many hubs are there and where are they located within the towns?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: So, together, not just with stakeholders, with prison or the Home Team, but also with the families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: So, what efforts are there that we can encourage families to play a more active role in the re-integration process of the desistors?

sections.label: Public perception of PolCams
sections.summary: In the latest public perception survey, nine in 10 Singaporeans said they see the value of PolCams.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In fact, in our latest public perception survey, nine in 10 Singaporeans said that they see the value of these PolCams.

sections.label: Attractive progression pathways
sections.summary: The passage states progression pathways must be well laid out and attractive, citing a new programme with the Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine on graduate certificates in advanced pre-hospital care.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The first is that the progression pathways have to be well laid out and they have to be attractive.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, one example is the new programme that we are working on with the Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine to develop graduate certificates in advanced pre-hospital care.

sections.label: Diploma in paramedicine programme
sections.summary: A diploma in paramedicine programme with PSB Academy will double the annual intake at diploma level.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: One example is the diploma in paramedicine programme, which we are working with the PSB Academy on.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This will double the annual intake at the diploma level.

sections.label: Paramedic and EMT certification tests
sections.summary: Paramedics must pass paramedic specialist and ambulance proficiency tests, and emergency medical technicians the SCDF EMT certification test, before deployment.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: All paramedics will also need to pass the paramedic specialist certification test and the ambulance proficiency test while emergency medical technicians will need to pass the SCDF Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) certification test before they are deployed.

sections.label: IMPACT framework replaces DORP
sections.summary: The IMPACT framework replaces DORP, rebranding and enhancing the DORP framework.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In place of DORP, we thought we could enhance the framework and as such, we came out with the IMPACT framework.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: It is a rebranding and at the same time, enhancement of the DORP framework.

sections.label: Collaboration with Social Service Institute
sections.summary: Under IMPACT, collaboration with the Social Service Institute aims to hone volunteer skills in befriending inmates and their families.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Under IMPACT, we formalise our collaboration with the Social Service Institute, where the aim is to hone volunteer skills in befriending and how they can work with the inmates and their families.

sections.label: Training spaces increase under IMPACT
sections.summary: In 2024, 3,200 training spaces were provided, and IMPACT can increase this to approximately 4,500 spaces per year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For example, in 2024, we provided 3,200 training spaces.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: But with IMPACT, we can increase it to approximately 4,500 spaces per year.

sections.label: Codes of practice under Online Criminal Harms Act
sections.summary: Two codes of practice, for online communication services and e-commerce services, are both under the Online Criminal Harms Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I had mentioned about the two codes of practices, namely one for the online communication services and the other for e-commerce services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: These are both under the Online Criminal Harms Act.

sections.label: Facebook Marketplace and Carousell losses
sections.summary: The speaker says early successes were seen with Facebook Marketplace and Carousell, with losses falling 10% for Carousell and 60% for Facebook Marketplace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I have also shared that we have seen some early successes with Facebook Marketplace, as well as with Carousell.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I have also indicated that we have seen losses in those areas for Carousell coming down by 10%, as well as for Facebook Marketplace coming down by 60%.

sections.label: Platform financial liability consideration
sections.summary: The speaker says making platforms financially liable for losses sustained on their platforms is something that can be considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the second question as to whether or not we want to consider whether or not these platforms should be made financially liable for losses that are sustained on their platforms, I think this is something that we can consider.

sections.label: Possible serious actions against Telegram
sections.summary: The speaker says Telegram takes anonymity as a badge of honour to users' detriment, options are being preserved, and serious actions will be considered if necessary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: With Telegram, unfortunately, it is a different story altogether.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: There are discussions internally as to what we should do with Telegram.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I had shared that they take anonymity on their platforms as a badge of honour, that works to the detriment of users.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, I think we are preserving some options now, thinking through, but if necessary, I think we will consider very serious actions against Telegram to ensure that they do not harm local citizens further.
